opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grant

deadlines.raw: 1 October 2026 (bi-monthly deadlines on the 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December)

amount.raw: Scheme A up to £200; Scheme B up to £500 (up to £750 for Adelphi co-sponsored award); Scheme C up to £300

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to Genetics Society 'junior scientist' members. Scheme A: undergraduate, Master's, PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva. Schemes B & C: PhD student and postdoctoral members within six years of PhD viva (not undergraduates/Master's). Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference; supervisor must be a current Genetics Society member.
opportunities.summary: Support for Genetics Society junior scientist members to attend conferences on genetics research. Scheme A: travel/accommodation to Genetics Society or SIG meetings (up to £200). Scheme B: travel, accommodation and registration at non-Genetics Society meetings (up to £500, or up to £750 for an Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award). Scheme C: registration costs for virtual conferences (up to £300).

opportunities.title: Training Grant

deadlines.raw: 15 November 2026 (quarterly deadlines at midnight on 15th February, May, August and November)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society who are studying or working in the UK, or attending a course held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others must be members for at least one year. A supporting letter from a supervisor (also a member) is required for students.
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,200 to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence and registration/tuition fees.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant

deadlines.raw: 1 November 2026 (quarterly deadlines at midnight on 1st February, May, August and November)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society who are studying or working in the UK, or intending to carry out fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become members; others must be members for at least one year. A supporting letter from a supervisor (also a member) is required for students.
opportunities.summary: Awards of up to £2,000, funded by income from the journal Heredity, to cover travel and accommodation costs associated with field-based genetic research projects whose results would be suitable for publication in Heredity. Covers travel, accommodation, subsistence, consumables for pre-processing and some essential field equipment.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement Grant

deadlines.raw: 1 October 2026 (two deadlines per year: 1st March and 1st October)

opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,000 to support public engagement activities related to genetics, delivered in person or virtually. Funding may be used for eligible travel (budget/economy class, UK-based only) and materials costs. Cannot be used for salaries, room hire in academic institutions, or activities already funded by UKRI/charity grants.

opportunities.title: Carer's Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any Genetics Society member, regardless of the age of the person they care for. Priority given to early-career scientists and according to need. Number of awards restricted based on anticipated event attendance.
opportunities.summary: Award of up to £60/day to support members with caring responsibilities to attend Society meetings and events, used as the applicant thinks best supports their attendance. Competitive; applied for prior to the meeting/event and claimed in arrears on production of electronic receipts.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting Sponsorship

amount.raw: Several levels: a Genetics Society lecture for a few hundred pounds, a Genetics Society session up to about £1,000, major sponsorship of an entire meeting potentially several thousand pounds (major sponsorship levels over the last 12 months £1,000-£2,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Members of the Genetics Society. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK. Grants are for the organisation of a meeting, not attendance.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic-themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society. Members may apply at any time of the year (at least three months in advance of the event). Applications reviewed at the end of each month; sponsorship must include a Carer's Award.

opportunities.title: Special Interest Group Funding
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Genetics research communities wishing to run regular series of themed meetings. Meetings should be based in, or have strong links with, the UK.
opportunities.summary: Funding of up to £2,000 per year for genetics research communities to run regular series of research meetings on particular themes. Applications to become a new Special Interest Group should be submitted at least three months before the date of the first meeting and include a funding proposal.
